extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and academics invited to peer review manuscripts for PLOS One
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers acting as peer reviewers for submissions to PLOS One, covering invitation acceptance, the peer review model, what to assess, review-writing, and policies for specific article types (Registered Reports, Protocols, Lab Protocols).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting an invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept an invitation only if you have the knowledge, time and objectivity necessary to provide an unbiased assessment of the research. In agreeing to complete a review, you also give permission to publish your review under a Creative Commons Attribution CC BY license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the links in the invitation email to accept or decline. If you cannot be objective, lack expertise, or lack time, decline. Be aware that your review may be published and will be shared with authors and other reviewers in the editorial decision letter; signing is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model and anonymity options
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS One practices single-anonymized peer review by default (reviewers know authors, authors do not know reviewers), but offers signed and published peer review options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may choose to sign your name to your review; if you sign it will appear with the review and, if authors publish peer review history, your name will accompany your comments. Reviews are portable between PLOS journals and may accompany manuscripts transferred between journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A competing interest is anything that interferes with or could be perceived as potentially interfering with, a thorough and objective assessment of a manuscript. Common examples include recent/current collaboration with authors, direct competition or history of scientific conflict, and opportunities to profit financially from the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept a review assignment if you have a competing interest or don’t feel able to give an objective assessment. If unsure, contact plosone@plos.org for advice. If asked to complete the review despite a potential competing interest, declare it when you submit your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crediting collaborators and co-reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-reviewing with a mentor or collaborator is encouraged as a learning activity, but if someone helped you complete the review you must share your collaborator’s name with the journal when you submit the review (enter it in question 2 under 'Confidential comments to Editor' or email the journal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include the co-reviewer's name in the text of the review itself. Competing interests and confidentiality policies apply to all reviewers. Failure to credit collaborators is a breach of policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep manuscripts and correspondence confidential and do not share information about submissions with anyone else unless previously agreed with the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make use of any material or take advantage of information gained through the peer review process. Read the PLOS Confidentiality Policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing a manuscript previously reviewed elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: If you reviewed the article at another journal, consider the manuscript as a new submission unless instructed otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in mind the manuscript may have been revised and PLOS One criteria may differ from the other journal. When you submit your review, let the editor know that you reviewed a previous version at another journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to complete your review within 10 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need more time, email the journal as soon as possible to request an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured reviewer form (how to submit answers)
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS One uses a structured reviewer form with two sections: Comments to the author and Comments to the editor. Answers to questions 1-4 are required (select from drop-down responses such as 'Yes,' 'No,' 'I don't know,' 'N/A') and you must provide details as needed. Enter the main text of your peer review in question 5, 'Review Comments to the Author.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments entered in the 'Comments to the author' section will be included in the decision letter to the author. The 'Comments to the editor' section is for declaring competing interests and listing collaborators; PLOS One does not allow confidential comments other than the declaration of competing interests. If you have confidential ethics concerns, contact plosone@plos.org directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: No confidential comments except competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS One does not allow confidential comments other than the declaration of competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have confidential concerns relating to publication or research ethics, contact plosone@plos.org. Do not place confidential concerns in the reviewer form unless they are competing interest declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication criterion: original research
rubrics_metrics.description: The study presents the results of original research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers should check that the manuscript reports new original work rather than republishing previously reported results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication criterion: results not published elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Results reported have not been published elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm there is no prior publication of the same results (duplicate publication). If prior versions exist, consider differences and disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication criterion: technical quality and methodological detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments, statistics, and other analyses are performed to a high technical standard and are described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess experimental design, statistical analyses, sample sizes, controls, and whether methods are described thoroughly enough for others to repeat the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication criterion: conclusions supported by data
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions are presented in an appropriate fashion and are supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the claims made are justified by the results and analyses; request additional evidence or analyses if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication criterion: intelligible presentation and standard English
rubrics_metrics.description: The article is presented in an intelligible fashion and is written in standard English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity, organization, and readability; indicate if language or presentation prevents understanding and suggest improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication criterion: ethics and research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The research meets all applicable standards for the ethics of experimentation and research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for appropriate ethical approvals, informed consent, humane treatment of animals, data integrity issues, and other ethics requirements. Flag any suspected ethical concerns to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication criterion: reporting guidelines and data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The article adheres to appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm relevant checklists (e.g., CONSORT, PRISMA) are followed, data are shared in suitable repositories, and accession/version numbers are provided for relevant resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports — Protocol-stage review
rubrics_metrics.description: For Registered Report Protocol submissions you will review study design, rationale, timeline, proposed methodology for data collection and analysis, and ethical approval plans. Peer review aims to ensure the proposed research is rigorous and that the methodology and analysis are sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider: Is the rationale clear and valid? Is the protocol technically sound and likely to achieve its aims and test stated hypotheses? Is the methodology feasible and described in sufficient detail to be replicable? Ensure peer review focuses on rigor and feasibility at the pre-results stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports — Results-stage review
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Registered Report results manuscript you will review the methods and findings of the study originally outlined in the Protocol, focusing on adherence to the Registered Report Protocol and appropriateness of any deviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider: Have authors followed the procedures in their protocol? If not, are deviations justified? Are any additional experiments or exploratory results reasonable and methodologically sound? Are conclusions supported by the data and address the original hypothesis?

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing Lab Protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Lab Protocols describe reusable methodologies; peer review ensures the manuscript complies with submission guidelines and publication criteria for Lab Protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider: Is the protocol of utility to the research community? Does it link to a protocols.io entry and is a PDF attached as supplementary information? Are methods and reagents described sufficiently? Are controls and sample sizes appropriate? Do authors demonstrate the method is validated (link to supporting peer-reviewed publication or supporting data)? If manuscript contains new data, has it been made fully available?

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing Study Protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Study Protocols are plans for studies not yet generating results; review aims to assess ability to test hypotheses, sufficiency of detail for replication, suitability of planned analysis, and writing quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider prerequisites (no completed data collection), required ethical standards, validity of rationale and research questions, technical soundness and feasibility, description sufficiency for replication, data availability plans, whether title contains the word 'Protocol', inclusion of recommended checklists as SI files, registration on an appropriate platform (e.g., OSF). For clinical trials, check registration in a WHO/ICMJE-approved registry and provision of a SPIRIT checklist and enrollment schedule. For systematic reviews, check provision and completeness of PRISMA-P checklist and registration (e.g., PROSPERO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the review — purpose and key questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The review should provide editors with an expert opinion on the validity and quality of the manuscript and give authors explicit feedback to improve the paper for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing, address: the main claims and their significance; placement of claims in context of literature and fairness to prior work; whether data and analyses fully support claims or what additional evidence is needed; whether detailed protocols/algorithms should be published as SI; if protocols are provided, whether deviations are adequately explained; whether the study shows sufficient potential to warrant resubmission; whether original data are deposited and accession numbers provided; conformity with relevant guidelines (CONSORT, MIAME, QUORUM, STROBE, Fort Lauderdale agreement, etc.); whether methods are sufficient for reproduction; availability of software created by authors; whether manuscript is well organized and accessible to non-specialists; and whether the manuscript contains an NIH-defined Dual Use concern. Direct remarks that will strengthen the paper to the authors rather than confidential editor comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions and re-review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are often asked to evaluate revised manuscripts and authors’ responses to reviewer comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asked, make yourself available for re-review and be prepared to assess whether authors have adequately addressed prior concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing reviewer reports policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Board members should not edit or delete reviewer reports; PLOS staff will not change any reviewer comments intended for authors except in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS staff may edit or remove reviewer text only when language is inappropriate for professional communication, or if the comments contain information considered confidential or would incur a major risk if conveyed to authors. If PLOS staff advise that comments can be disregarded, they may inform authors. Authors should contact the journal office with concerns about feedback in decision letters. See COPE guidance referenced for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision process and handling conflicting reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors make the final decision on whether to publish based on reviewers’ comments, PLOS One criteria for publication, and the editor's own assessment. Conflicting reviews may be handled by sharing reviews with reviewers and requesting additional comments; decisions are not strictly by majority rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors evaluate reviewer recommendations alongside authors' comments and any additional material. Experts may disagree; the editor synthesizes evidence to reach a decision. Reviewers should know their recommendation will be considered but the final decision rests with the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer credit (ORCID)
rubrics_metrics.description: Link your PLOS reviewer account to your ORCID record to have reviewer activity posted to your ORCID profile review activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This records that you completed a review for the journal but does not publish the content of your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirement: submit reviews via the system
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be entered in the submission system (Editorial Manager).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have trouble accessing the manuscript or entering comments, email the journal office for assistance. Use the 'New Reviewer Invitations' folder to find invitations.
